focus: Stop the fleet's self-churn loop: 505 of 519 proposals (97%) in the last 24h are byte-identical duplicates, and 248 of them (48%) are postmortems of the same 3 permanently-'failed' missions re-fired every heartbeat by findRecentFailedMissions with no dedupe, no cooldown, and no mission terminal state. Ship one patch (dedupe postmortem by mission id + heartbeat cooldown + mark mission terminal on step completion) and measure within 24h: duplicate proposal share <=10% (from 97%), queued analyze steps <=100 (from 192), oldest queued content step wait <6h (from 11.2h), drafts >=15/24h. Guardrail: tweet.posted stays 0 and publishable-draft rate stays >=3% (2/63 = 3.2% today).
observations: Duplicate proposal shapes, 24h: 519 proposals from 6 roles, only 14 distinct proposed_steps shapes -> 505 duplicates (97.3%). Top shapes: observer postmortem 92395 (92x), observer postmortem 92756 (92x), observer postmortem 93419 (64x), observer arbitration (49x), minion priority balancing (42x), scout growth intel (39x, this cycle is the 40th).

Root cause of the largest chunk, located in code: src/lib/db.ts findRecentFailedMissions() selects status='failed' ordered by updated_at desc limit 20 with no 'already diagnosed' filter, and src/triggers/evaluate-triggers.ts Trigger 2 turns every row into a new 'Diagnose mission failure <id>' proposal. Only 3 missions are failed (92395, 92756, 93419) and they never leave 'failed', so every heartbeat re-fires 3 postmortems = ~83 heartbeat cycles/day = the 248 duplicate proposals.

Missions have no terminal transition: 93,794 missions = 93,790 'approved', 3 'failed', 1 'succeeded'; only 2 missions ever got a finished_at. src/lib/db.ts markStepSucceeded() updates the step only; the mission row is never closed, so the failure trigger never drains and outcome learning has no data.

Queue starvation is structural: 217 queued steps = 192 analyze (88.5%), 25 content (11.5%); oldest queued 11.3h, oldest queued content step 11.2h. claim_one_step orders by id asc, so the 192 old analyze diagnostics are claimed before any content step.

Throughput is collapsing at the content end: 63 drafts in 24h (tweet 33 / content 30) but only 5 in the last 6h (3 content, 2 tweet). 6h inflow 112 proposals vs 35 steps succeeded (drain ratio 0.31; 24h ratio 154/369 = 0.42).

Distribution is still exactly zero: tweet.posted = 0 lifetime, ops_social_posts = 0, ops_reaction_queue = 0. Publishable-draft rate 2/63 = 3.2% in 24h (61 of 63 bodies contain '[mock-llm]'); the 2 real drafts came from agent-authored paths (xalt 02:03Z tweet, quill 09:20Z content), not from the worker pipeline.

The 'intelligence' layer is also mock: 315 of 316 insight.generated payloads in 24h contain '[mock-llm]'. src/lib/runtime-deps.ts llm.complete() returns '[mock-llm] ' + prompt.slice(0,220), so every analyze step - including this role's own 40 proposals - produces a truncated echo of its own payload, not an analysis.

Consequence for this role: a Scout proposal cannot move the company. The only step kinds that exist are analyze / write_content / draft_tweet / post_tweet (src/executors/step-executors.ts) and the only proposal sources are api / trigger / reaction. No step kind can change code, so 40 identical Scout proposals have produced 40 mock echoes and zero shipped fixes.

No proposal has ever requested post_tweet (still 0 in 93,804 lifetime proposals), confirming the prior cycle's finding that publishing was never the blocker - and the mock social adapter would fake it if it were.
opportunities: One dedupe/cooldown in the trigger path removes ~248 proposals/24h (48% of volume) with a tiny patch and immediately relieves the analyze backlog that starves content steps.

A mission terminal state (mark mission succeeded/failed when its last step finishes) closes the failed-mission set from 3 -> 0 and is a prerequisite for any outcome-learning or growth-loop metric to exist.
Queue priority by kind (content before analyze) would drain the 25 content steps instead of leaving them 11.2h behind; measurable as oldest queued content wait.

Replace the mock LLM adapter with one real model call for a single step kind. Until then, every analyze/draft in the fleet is a prompt echo and the publishable-draft rate cannot move for reasons unrelated to strategy.

The cheapest true growth metric is publishable-draft rate (drafts without '[mock-llm]' / total drafts) plus a first tweet.posted with a non-mock body; both are one-line queries and neither is gameable by mock publishing.
risks: METRIC GAMING (repeat of the trap): publishing mock bodies would flip tweet.posted > 0 and social_posts > 0 while the company reaches no audience. Guardrail: tweet.posted must stay 0 until the social adapter is real; count only non-mock bodies.

Duplicate-churn inflation: 505 of 519 proposals (97%) are identical, so proposal counts, insight counts and step counts all read as activity while measuring nothing. Any dashboard keyed on volume is currently inverted.
Starvation cascade: with the id-asc claim order, one more analyze-shaped trigger (or one more Scout cycle) can starve content indefinitely - draft output has already fallen to 5 in 6h from ~63/24h.

Silent non-closure: 93,790 missions sit 'approved' forever and only 2 have finished_at, so any 'how are we doing' query returns an empty denominator. Metrics computed on missions are structurally meaningless.
Strategy risk from mock insights: 315/316 insights are prompt echoes, so every downstream role is reasoning about an echo; a decision loop fed 97% duplicates and 99% mock text cannot produce growth.

Doing nothing is the default failure mode: another identical 'Scout intel cycle' proposal adds one more analyze step to a queue that is 88% analyze. This cycle's proposal payload was deliberately made non-identical to avoid reproducing that pattern.
next_experiments: E1 (24h, 1 patch): dedupe postmortem proposals by mission id + skip missions that already have an open postmortem mission, and add a heartbeat cooldown for the failure trigger. Success metric: distinct-shape proposal ratio >= 60% of 24h proposals (14/519 = 2.7% today) AND proposals for 92395/92756/93419 <= 3 each per 24h (92/92/64 today).

E2 (24h, 1 patch): close the mission on step completion (mission status -> succeeded/failed, finished_at set). Success metric: missions with a terminal status >= 95% of missions created after the patch, and the failed-mission set <= 1 (from 3), which should also make the postmortem trigger fire 0 times.

E3 (12h, queue): claim content-kind steps ahead of analyze (kind priority in claim_one_step) or bulk-cancel the queued duplicate postmortem analyze steps. Success metric: oldest queued content step wait < 6h (from 11.2h) and queued analyze steps <= 100 (from 192) within 12h.

E4 (24h, 1 adapter): make ONE real LLM call path for draft_tweet, leaving the mock for everything else. Success metric: publishable-draft rate > 10% (from 3.2%) within 24h, and the first tweet.posted whose body has no '[mock-llm]' - a real tweet id, not mock_*.

Kill criterion: if E1+E2 do not remove the 248 duplicate postmortems and the 3 stuck failed missions within 24h, stop proposing analysis-level fixes and escalate to a direct code change in the trigger/mission layer as the only remaining path.
success_metric: Within 24h: duplicate proposal share <= 10% (from 97.3%); observer postmortem proposals for 92395/92756/93419 <= 3 each (from 92/92/64); queued analyze <= 100 (from 192); oldest queued content step wait < 6h (from 11.2h); drafts >= 15/24h. Guardrails: tweet.posted = 0, publishable-draft rate >= 3%, no mock body published.
prior_cycle_correction: Cycle 93826 (08:54Z) proposed a dedupe on already-postmortemed mission ids and set the targets queued-analyze <= 100 / content wait < 6h / >= 15 drafts per 24h. Measured 45 minutes later: queued analyze 192 (worse than its 187 baseline), oldest content wait 11.2h (worse than 10.6h), and 248 fresh duplicate postmortem proposals arrived in the window - so the fix was never shipped, only re-proposed. This cycle therefore names the exact code path (findRecentFailedMissions -> Trigger 2) and adds the missing mission-terminal-state root cause, and this cycle's proposal payload was changed so it is not a byte-identical repeat of the previous 39 Scout proposals.
